narrative:
MAJOR REGULATIONS
PREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Up to 8 units of UD CCS courses and Music 188 may be taken P/NP, with no more than 3 units from Music 188. All other major units, including those applied to the major from other departments, must be taken for letter grades.
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS With the approval of each department chairperson, up to a total of 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

nodes.title: Careers in Music
nodes.description: Through lectures, discussions, and guest speakers, this course introduces students to various career options in music and the arts, including a practical overview of the skills, knowledge and paths to pursue these goals, culminating in students developing a career portfolio.

nodes.title: Introduction to Music Studies
nodes.description: Introduces students to ways of studying music as a cultural practice situated in society. Methods are drawn from musicology, ethnomusicology, history, anthropology, and sociology. Students will be taught to think critically about music as a universal human expression.

nodes.title: Structures of Music
nodes.prereq_text: Open to Music and Music Studies majors, or by consent of instructor. Music minors to contact instructor or advisor for approval.

items.text: Open to Music and Music Studies majors, or by consent of instructor

nodes.description: Looking at a variety of music traditions from different parts of the world, the class will survey varying approaches to issues of compositional structure, rhythm, intonation, scales, etc. The class will have listening and practical components.

nodes.title: Music Theory and Practice I
nodes.description: Theory basics, including rhythm and meter, pitch, intervals, scales, keys, triads, seventh chords, and essentials of harmonic progression.

nodes.description: Textural deployments of harmony, tonic and dominant on the small and large scale, contrapuntal influences, cadential progressions, non-chord tones.

nodes.prereq_text: Placement exam or Music 5B with a grade of at least C-. Must be taken consecutively, and concurrently with the Music 4 series.

nodes.title: History of Western Music from Early Modern Culture through Modernism
nodes.description: A survey of Western music and its social contexts from late humanism through the Age of Enlightenment (1545-1745). Topics include Renaissance legacies, music and religious reformations, ancient vs. modern, the rise of opera, patronage, instrumental composer-performers, taste in the Enlightenment.

nodes.title: History of Western Music from Early Modern Culture through Modernism
nodes.description: A survey of Western music and its social contexts from 1745 to 1848. Topics include the rise of public concerts and of the virtuoso soloist, the evolution of the orchestra, music in salons and parlors, and national operatic institutions.

nodes.title: History of Western Music from Early Modern Culture through Modernism
nodes.description: A survey of Western music and its social contexts from 1848 to 1945. Topics include music and nationalism, late romanticism and the limits of tonality, modernism, the impact of popular music on art music, and neoclassicism.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Music
nodes.description: The study of notes, scales, triads, inversions, rhythm, harmony, and musical terminology. Laboratory activities include keyboard orientation, sight singing, and ear training.

nodes.title: Thinking Historically about Music
nodes.description: This course reflects on the process of crafting narratives about the musical past and its impact on our understanding of music in the present. Students learn to analyze diverse sources and practice the construction of music historical narratives.

nodes.title: Constructing Communities through Music: Classical and Beyond
nodes.description: Examines how music builds and sustains communities across historical contexts. Students develop critical and historical thinking using case studies from Europe and the United States to explore musical practices (classical and beyond), socio-economic contexts, and continuities between past and present.

nodes.title: Listening to Jazz: Demystifying Americas Musical Art Form
nodes.description: Aims to unravel the mystery of Jazzs allure, importance, and performance process, in a manner mostly divorced from technical musical terminology or music theory, through targeted readings, listening assignments, written projects, in-class visits, and concert attendance.

nodes.title: World Music
nodes.description: An introductory course surveying the unity and diversity of folk, traditional, and classical music of the non-western world. Emphasis given to dance, theatre, musical instruments, and the role of music in society.

nodes.title: Introduction to Electroacoustic Music Thought
nodes.description: An introductory course on electroacoustic music. Historical perspective. Analysis of different types of electronic/acousmatic/mixed compositions. Introduction to different techniques of sound transformation.

nodes.title: Real-Time Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition.
nodes.description: First quarter of a 3-quarter series course in real-time digital synthesis and composition will concentrate on multi-track recording, mixing, digital signal processing using micro-computers and special purpose DSP equipment for music composition.

nodes.title: Real-Time Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition
nodes.description: Second quarter of a 3-quarter series course will concentrate on digital synthesis (primarily frequency modulation, simple and complex; but also amplitude modulation and additive synthesis) using micro-computers, digital synthesizers and processing equipment for music composition.

nodes.title: Real-Time Digital Synthesis, Processing and Composition

nodes.title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1545-1745
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations from Renaissance through Enlightenment (1545-1745). Topics include musicians’ careers and social life; spirituality; gender, race, emerging subjectivity; music for public stages; commercialism; colonialism; popular music practices. Western music notation experience required.

nodes.title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1745-1848
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations 1748-1848. Topics include a range of composers/performers/listeners and how conceptions of musical practices were shaped by socio-political context, colonialism, class, gender, race, religion, economics. Western music notation experience required.

nodes.title: History of Western Music and its Global Circulations, 1848-1945
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Explores history of western music and its global circulations 1848-1945, including its philosophical, artistic, and social contexts. Topics include nationalism; late romanticism and limits tonality; modernism; impact of popular music on western classical music; neoclassicism. Western music notation experience required.

nodes.title: The History of Opera: 1600-1800
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: An overview of the history of opera from 1600-1800, placing selected works within a social context, and viewing opera as a musical work, dramatic spectacle, and cultural commodity.

nodes.title: Music and Popular Culture in America
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A survey of the relationships between music and popular culture in America. Music to be discussed includes blues, jazz, and rock, as well as classical music. Emphasis is on cultural, rather than technical aspects of music.

nodes.title: Symphonic Music
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.prereq_text: Music 15 or Music 3A. Music 3A may be taken concurrently.
nodes.description: A study of selected symphonic works.

nodes.title: American Music History: From the Colonial Period to the Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: An overview of the varieties of American musical experience from the Colonial period to the present. Representative works from several genres are studies with a view to placing them in their cultural context and identifying major aesthetic issues.

nodes.title: American Experimental Music: John Cage and After
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A survey of the American experimental tradition in music and related arts, starting with John Cage and continuing through generations of those have followed in his path through the present day. Students will read primary sources by these artists as well as secondary literature from theoretical and historical perspectives; course activities will also include study and discussion of experimental artworks, written responses, and creative activities.

nodes.title: Music and the Mind
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Introduction to the psychology of music. Topics include music perception and cognition, learning and memory, emotion and meaning, music and language, music and the brain, emergence and development of skills, perspectives from social and cultural psychology, well-being and therapy, and others.

nodes.title: Music and Politics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A study of the interaction between music and politics from the fourteenth century to the present. Includes discussion of relevant art from each period.

nodes.title: Tuning and Temperament
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.	Materials and Techniques
nodes.description: Survey of a number of tuning systems found around the world, including those of Ancient Greece, Europe, India, China, the Arab Middle East, Turkey, and Indonesia. The mathematical, aesthetic, and symbolic bases of each system will be considered.

nodes.title: The Arabic System of Melodic Modes: The Maqamat
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.	Materials and Techniques
nodes.description: An intensive examination of the system of melodic modes (Maqamat) that governs present-day practice in the eastern Arab world. Emphasis given to theoretical issues (quarter tones, tetrachordel structures, and theories of intonation), analysis of standard repertoire, and procedures governing improvisation.

nodes.title: Analysis of Popular Music
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: B.	Materials and Techniques
nodes.prereq_text: Music 5B with a grade of at least C-
nodes.description: Explores different approaches to analyzing popular music (specifically post-1960, predominantly American popular music), including not only theory and analysis of harmony and melody, form, timbre, rhythm/meter but also issues of meanings and expression, intertextuality, race and gender.

nodes.title: Choral Literature
nodes.prereq_text: Three quarters of the Music 112A-F series.

requires.text: Three quarters of the MUS 112A-F series

nodes.description: A historical and analytical survey of major choral works from the seventeenth century to the present.

nodes.title: Other Issues in Ethnomusicology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A study of other cultural issues in ethnomusicology. Specific issue or topics will vary by quarter and will be announced in advance by the department.

nodes.title: Film Music Cognition
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A consideration of film music as a medium of communication between the director, composer, music supervisor, editors, performers and the audience. Emphasis given to cognitive psychological theories of meaning in terms of structure and affect in audio/visual contexts.

nodes.title: Music and Documentary Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: View global popular music through the lens of documentary film. We will analyze a series of films depicting cultural and political histories, creative performances, and everyday lives of musicians in different representational frames and social contexts.

nodes.title: Creative Arts, Memories and Experimental Performance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Through creative arts practices, analysis, workshops and new performance, this course explores processes of transformation and translation of traces of memories and experiences into provocative art works. Experimental performance practices encompass theatrical, movement based, sonic, music-based and visual arts.

nodes.title: Music and Sports
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: In this course, students study connections between the human cultural practices of music and sport. We draw from rich literatures in performance studies, sports studies, and ethnomusicology to consider selected case studies where music and sport intersect.

nodes.title: Birds, sonic arts & environmental sensitivities
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Focusing on birds and sonic arts, this course engages creative, analytical & experiential activities. Topics include: ecoacoustics, sound maps, deep listening, sensory memory, soundscape ecologies and environmental issues, blurring borders between more-than-human/human interactions, art/science, and local/global.

nodes.title: Umm Kulthum: Her Music, Her Life, Her Times
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Analysis of the music, life, an times of the predominant Arab singer of the twentieth century. Individual projects may focus on music or text analysis, issues of gender, nationalism, agency, performance practice, and investigation of related arts (film, novels, etc.).

nodes.title: Music Cultures of the World: The Middle East
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Arab, Turkish, and Persian music traditions from historical, cultural, and musicological perspectives. Emphasis given to the position of music in Islam, present-day performers, and modal and rhythmic structures.

nodes.title: Music Cultures of the World: India
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A survey of music traditions of the Indian subcontinent from classical to folk and popular. Emphasis on the position of music in Hindu philosophy, the role of music in society, musical instruments, and modal and rhythmic structures (Raga and Tala).

nodes.title: Music in Modern Japan
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: This course explores music and culture in modern Japan. What kind of society do we hear in its diverse mix of sounds and musical practices? We explore this question through traditional genres, national politics, and transnational exchanges of popular media.

nodes.title: Music Cultures of the World: Other Regions
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A study of music traditions and genres from other regions of the world. Specific regions studied vary by quarter and are announced in advance by the department.

nodes.title: Environmental Sound Arts
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing, instructor approval required.
nodes.description: Environmental Sound Arts focuses on responses to, and uses of environmental sounds in the broadest framework of soundscapes and environmental humanities, encompassing processes of fieldwork listening , analysis, and creation of new environmental sound art for public facing advocacy work.

nodes.title: Music, Community, Wellbeing: Advocacy and Activism
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: Taking a vocational and facilitatory approach, this course uses case studies to explore concepts and processes of generating and sustaining musical activity as community-engaged practice. Topics include: social justice, health and wellbeing, education, senses of place, ecology, and technology.

nodes.title: Studies in Ethnomusicology
nodes.description: An introduction to the field of ethnomusicology using theories and methods derived from the social sciences and humanities. Topic areas to include transcription and analysis, musicians, musical instruments, music acculturation, and the function of music in society.

nodes.title: Proseminar in Classical Music
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of classical music.

nodes.title: Proseminar in Romantic Music
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of romantic music.

nodes.title: Proseminar in Contemporary Music
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: A. History and Culture
nodes.description: A selective study of various stylistic and historical aspects of contemporary music.

nodes.title: Ethnomusicology Forum
nodes.description: A forum for the presentation of research and performance by students, faculty, and visiting scholars and performers.

nodes.description: Special seminar in selected problems of current musicology, ethnomusicology, theory, or performance.

nodes.title: Individual Research in Music
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor.

items.text: completion of three quarters of the MUS 112AB-F series

nodes.description: Independent research under the guidance of a faculty member in the department. Course offers qualified students the opportunity to undertake independent research or work in a research group in topics in musicology, ethnomusicology, composition, theory, or performance.

nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of three quarters of the Music 112AB-F series; consent of instructor and department.

nodes.title: Wind Ensemble
nodes.prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.
nodes.description: Masterworks of the literature for ensembles smaller than orchestral or full band scoring. Although the basic ensembles feature winds, both strings and percussion are utilized.

nodes.title: UCSB Chamber Choir
nodes.description: A select ensemble of voice majors and non-majors, the Chamber Choir prepares musicians for professional ensemble work and offers advanced study in choral literature, techniques, styles and interpretation covering five centuries of choral repertoire.

nodes.title: UCSB Concert Choir
nodes.description: The UCSB Concert Choir is a mixed-voice ensemble open to all voice types (SATB). No audition required. Singers build musicianship and ensemble skills through diverse repertoire, weekly rehearsals, and public performances.

nodes.title: UCSB Singing Gauchos
nodes.description: The UCSB Singing Gauchos is a tenor and bass choir performing fine choral literature representative of various style periods and vocal techniques from the global choral tradition. Regular performances on and off campus.

nodes.title: Opera Workshop
nodes.description: Participation in opera scenes.

nodes.title: Ensemble for Contemporary Music
nodes.prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.
nodes.description: Reading sessions and preparation for performance of contemporary music. There will be one or two concerts each quarter. Includes departmental scholarship players, and is open to composers who also perform.

nodes.title: Piano Ensemble
nodes.prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. Upper-division students only.
nodes.description: Piano duets (1 piano, 4 hands) and duos (2 pianos) in separate sections.

nodes.title: Orchestra
nodes.prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.
nodes.description: UCSB Chamber Orchestra performs pieces from the traditional chamber orchestra repertoire, as well as more contemporary pieces for chamber orchestra.

nodes.title: Flute Choir
nodes.description: The flute choir studies flute literature in depth, perfects technique and interpretation, employs the complete flute family of bass, alto flutes and piccolos. Prepares ensemble for public performances each quarter.

nodes.title: Chamber Music Ensemble
nodes.prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.
nodes.description: Chamber music ensemble.

nodes.title: Brass Quintet
nodes.description: Participation in scholarship brass quintet.

nodes.title: Brass Orchestral Repertoire
nodes.description: Intensive exploration of staple brass orchestral repertoire, emphasizing the works of important 19th and 20th century composers. Classes include rehearsal sessions, guided listening and analysis, mock auditions, resume and taped audition preparation.

nodes.title: Horn Ensemble
nodes.description: Horn ensemble.

nodes.title: Jazz Ensemble
nodes.description: Instruction in interpretation and performance of jazz music. Improvisation is stressed.

nodes.title: Percussion Ensemble
nodes.prereq_text: Enrollment by audition. For upper-division students.
nodes.description: Rehearsal and performance of standard percussion ensemble literature. Instruction of appropriate playing techniques for standard and exotic percussion instruments.

nodes.title: Cello Choir
nodes.description: The cello choir studies cello literature in depth, including duos, trios, quartets and larger cello ensemble works. Cellists work together on blend of sound, perfecting technique and intonation, as well as balance.The choir will prepare works for public performances.
